Στίχ. ʹ. Ἐὰν ἀναβῇ εἰς οὐρανὸν αὐτοῦ τὰ δῶρα· ἡ δὲ θυσία αὐτοῦ νεφῶν ἅψηται. Τοῦ
ἀσεβοῦς ἐὰν ἀναβῇ τὰ δῶρα εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν, ἐὰν πάνυ ὑψωθῇ, ἐὰν ἡ θυσία αὐτοῦ
νεφῶν ἅψηται. Ὅτ' ἂν εὔξηται ὁ αἱρετικὸς, ὅτ' ἂν ἡ θυσία αὐτοῦ ἀναβῇ τῇ
ὑψηγορίᾳ, ὅτ' ἂν δοκῇ κατεστηρίχθαι· τότε εἰς τέλος ἀπολεῖται. Ἡ γὰρ εὐχὴ αὐτοῦ
λο γίζεται αὐτῷ εἰς ἁμαρτίαν, καὶ ἔστιν αὐτὴ ἡ εὐχὴ αὐτοῦ ἁμαρτία. Στίχ. ζʹ. Ὅταν
γὰρ δοκῇ ἤδη ἐστηρίχθαι, τότε εἰς τέλος ἀπολεῖται. Ὅμοιον, Οἱ δὲ ἐχθροὶ τοῦ Κυρίου
ἅμα τῷ δοξα σθῆναι καὶ ὑψωθῆναι, ἐκλείποντες ὡσεὶ καπνὸς ἐξέλιπον. Στίχ. ζʹ. Οἱ δὲ
ἰδόντες αὐτὸν ἐροῦσι· Ποῦ ἔστιν; Τίνες οἱ ἰδόντες αὐτόν; Οἱ ἐκκλησιαστικοὶ, οἱ
ἰδόντες ἐκείνων τὰ σφάλματα, ἐροῦμεν· Ποῦ ἔστιν; Στίχ. ηʹ. Ὥσπερ ἐνύπνιον
ἐκπετασθὲν οὐ μὴ εὑρεθῇ. Οἱ τοιοῦτοι ἐνυπνιαζόμενοι, καὶ ἀναπλάσσοντες
φαντάσματα, οὐ τῇ ἀληθείᾳ τὴν διάνοιαν ἐπερείδου σιν σφαλλόμενοι, καὶ γίνονται
ὥσπερ ἐνύπνιον ἐκπετασθὲν, ὃ οὐ μὴ εὑρεθῇ. Στίχ. ιʹ. Τοὺς υἱοὺς αὐτοῦ ὀλέσαισαν
ἥττονες. Τοὺς υἱοὺς καὶ μαθητὰς τοῦ ταῦτα διδάξαντος. Στίχ. ιʹ. Αἱ δὲ χεῖρες αὐτοῦ
πυρσεύσαισαν ὀδύνας. Αἱ χεῖρες αὐτοῦ, φησὶν, τουτέστιν αἱ πράξεις, ἐξά ψουσιν
αὐτῷ κόλασιν. Αἱ δὲ χεῖρες αὐτοῦ. Τοῦ ἀσεβοῦς τούτου καὶ ἐσφαλμένου, οὗ ἡ
προσευχὴ λογίζεται εἰς ἁμαρ τίαν, οὗ ἡ θυσία ἐὰν ἀναβῇ εἰς οὐρανὸν, καὶ νε 17.73
φῶν ἅψηται, τότε εἰς τέλος ἀπόλλυται· τούτου αἱ χεῖρες ὀδύνας πυρσεύσουσι·
τουτέστι, καὶ ἐν ὀδύναις ἐσχάταις διάξουσι. Λέγει δὲ περὶ τῶν υἱῶν τοῦ πα ρανόμου.
Στίχ. ιγʹ. Χολὴ ἀσπίδος ἐν γαστρὶ αὐτοῦ. Ἔχει γὰρ μαθήματα, ἃ οὐκ ἔστι γλυκέα,
ἀλλὰ χολὴ ἀσπίδος, οἱονεὶ πονηρὰ, ἡ περὶ τοῦ οἴνου τῆς διδασκαλίας αὐτῶν. Ἐκ γὰρ
ἀμπέλου Σοδόμων ἡ ἄμπελος αὐτῶν, καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς. Καὶ μετ' ὀλίγα· Χολὴ δὲ ἀσπίδος ἐν
γαστρὶ τοῦ ἑτεροδόξου, καὶ ἀσεβοῦντος ἐν τοῖς δόγμασι, τοῖς ἐναντίοις τῇ ἀληθείᾳ.
Στίχ. ιεʹ. Πλοῦτος ἀδίκως συναγόμενος ἐξε μεθήσεται. Τίς γὰρ ἄλλος ἀδίκως πλοῦτος
συνάγεται ἢ ἐκεῖ νος ὁ ἐν τοῖς λόγοις αὐτῶν; Ἀδίκως γὰρ συνάγεται. Ἀλλ' ὁ ἀγαθὸς
οὐκ ἐάσει αὐτοὺς πεπτωκότας, πλοῦ τον ἀδίκως συναγόμενον ἔχειν ἀεὶ αὐτὸν ἐν
ἑαυτοῖς· ποιήσει γὰρ ἐξεμέσαι. Στίχ. ιεʹ. Ἐξ οἰκίας αὐτοῦ ἐξελκύσει αὐτὸν ἄγγελος.
Ἄγγελος γὰρ κατ' ἐνέργειαν καὶ εὐεργεσίαν τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐξελκύσει αὐτὸν ἀπ' αὐτῆς τῆς
κακῶς οἰκοδο μηθείσης, ἥτις ἐστὶν ἐκκλησία πονηρευομένων. Αὕτη γὰρ ἡ οἰκία
αὐτοῦ. Ἀλλ' ἄγγελος ἐξελκύσει αὐτὸν ἐξ οἰκίας αὐτοῦ. Στίχ. ιζʹ. Μὴ ἴδοι ἄμελξιν
νομάδων. Ἑτερόδοξος οὐ βλέπει ἄμελξιν νομάδων. Νο μάδες δὲ εἰσί τινες ψυχαὶ
νεμόμεναι ὑπὸ τῷ καλῷ Ποιμένι, τῷ εἰπόντι· Ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ θύρα. ∆ι' ἐμοῦ ἐάν τις
εἰσέλθῃ, σωθήσεται. Καὶ εἰσελεύσεται, καὶ ἐξελεύσεται, καὶ νομὴν εὑρήσει. Στίχ. ιηʹ.
Ὥσπερ στρίφνος ἀμάσητος, ἀκατά ποτος. Οἱ λόγοι καὶ τὰ δόγματα στριφνὰ καὶ
πυκνὰ, οὐ δὲν ἔχει γλυκὺ ἐκεῖνα, τὰ κατὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ γινόμενα. Στρίφνος βοτάνη, τίς
ἐστιν ἐκτραχυνομένη τῇ γλώσσῃ τοῦ μασσωμένου. Ὥσπερ οὖν, φησὶ, τὴν βοτάνην
ἐκείνην, κἂν ἄγαν τις φιλονεικήσειε διαλεά νας τοῖς ὀδοῦσι, καταπιεῖν οὐ δύναται·
οὕτω καὶ ὁ τῶν ἀλλοτρίων ἀπολαύειν ἐθέλων οὐδὲν τῶν πόνων ἀποίσεται τὸ
κέρδος. Στίχ. κʹ. ∆ιὰ τοῦτο οὐκ ἀνθήσει αὐτοῦ τὰ ἀγαθά. Ἂ δοκεῖ ἀγαθὰ ποιεῖν, οὐκ
ἀνθήσει· ὅτ' ἂν δοκῇ ἤδη πεπληρῶσθαι, θλιβήσεται. Στίχ. κʹ. Οὐκ ἔστιν αὐτοῦ
σωτηρία τοῖς ὑπάρχουσι. Τὰ ὑπάρχοντα αὐτοῦ σωτηρίαν αὐτῷ περιποιῆσαι οὐ
δύναται. Ἄλλως. Στίχ. κβʹ. Πᾶσα δὲ ἀνάγκη αὐτὸν ἐπελεύσεται, καὶ ἐπαποστελεῖ ἐπ'
αὐτὸν θυμὸν ὀργῆς. Στίχ. κβʹ. Πᾶσα δὲ ἀνάγκη ἐπ' αὐτὸν ἐπελεύ σεται. Ταῦτα
προτρεπτικὰ ἡμῖν, ἵνα ἀφιστώμεθα τῶν ἀλλοτρίων. 17.76 Στίχ. κβʹ. Νίψαι ἐπ' αὐτὸν
ὀδύνας. Ἀντὶ νιφετοῦ ὀδύναι ἔρχονται ἐπὶ τὸν τοιοῦτον. Στίχ. κδʹ. Καὶ οὐ μὴ σωθῇ ἐκ
χειρὸς σιδήρου. Σίδηρον οὐ λέγει τοῦτον τὸν αἰσθητὸν, ἀλλὰ τμη τικώτατον λόγον.
pass_a_gloss: Verse: If his gifts go up into heaven; and his sacrifice touches clouds. Of the impious — if his gifts go up into heaven, if they are very highly exalted, if his sacrifice touches clouds. Whenever the heretic prays, whenever his sacrifice goes up by high-speaking, whenever he seems to have been fixed firm — then he will be destroyed utterly. For his prayer is reckoned to him unto sin, and the prayer itself is sin. Verse 7: For when he already seems to have been fixed, then he will be destroyed utterly. Similar: But the enemies of the Lord, together with being glorified and exalted, failing as smoke they failed. Verse 7: And those who see him will say: Where is he? Who are those who see him? We church people, who see their errors, will say: Where is he? Verse 8: Like a dream that has flown away, it will not be found. Such people dreaming and molding fantasies do not rest the mind on the truth, being mistaken, and become like a dream flown away, which will not be found. Verse 10: Let lesser ones destroy his sons. The sons and disciples of the one who taught these things. Verse 10: And let his hands light pains as with a torch. His hands, it says — that is, the deeds — will kindle punishment for him. And his hands. Of this impious and mistaken one, whose prayer is reckoned unto sin, whose sacrifice if it goes up into heaven and touches clouds 17.73 then is utterly destroyed — of this one the hands will torch pains; that is, they will also spend time in last pains. And he speaks concerning the sons of the lawless one. Verse 13: Gall of an asp is in his belly. For he has teachings which are not sweet, but gall of an asp — as it were wicked — that about the wine of their teaching. For from the vine of Sodom is their vine, and the rest. And a little later: But gall of an asp is in the belly of the heterodox one, and of the one being impious in the doctrines opposite to the truth. Verse 15: Wealth gathered unjustly will be vomited out. For what other wealth is gathered unjustly than that in their words? For it is gathered unjustly. But the good one will not allow them, having fallen, to have wealth gathered unjustly always in themselves; for he will make [them] vomit it out. Verse 15: From his house an angel will drag him out. For an angel, according to the energy and beneficence of God, will drag him out from that very house badly built, which is a church of those doing evil. For this is his house. But an angel will drag him out from his house. Verse 17: May he not see milking of pastures. A heterodox one does not see milking of pastures. And pastures are certain souls pastured under the good Shepherd, who said: I am the door. Through me if someone enters, he will be saved. And he will go in, and go out, and find pasture. Verse 18: Like tough herb unchewed, unswallowable. The words and the doctrines are tough and dense; those things done against God have nothing sweet. Tough-herb is a plant, which is roughened by the tongue of the one chewing. As therefore, he says, that plant, even if someone contends very much, having smoothed it with the teeth, he cannot swallow it down; so also the one wanting to enjoy alien things will carry away no profit of the toils. Verse 20: For this reason his good things will not bloom. What he seems to do as good will not bloom; whenever he already seems to have been filled, he will be afflicted. Verse 20: There is no salvation of his for the belongings. His belongings cannot procure salvation for him. Otherwise. Verse 22: And every necessity will come upon him, and he will send upon him wrath of anger. Verse 22: And every necessity will come upon him. These things are hortatory for us, so that we may stand away from alien things. 17.76 Verse 22: Wash pains upon him. Instead of a snowstorm, pains come upon such a one. Verse 24: And he will not be saved from a hand of iron. He does not mean this perceptible iron, but a most cutting word.
pass_b_english: "[[If his gifts go up into heaven and his sacrifice touches the clouds >> Bible:Job 20:6]]" — even of the impious. When a heretic prays, when sacrifice rises by high-speaking, when he seems fixed firm, then he is destroyed utterly. "[[His prayer is reckoned to him as sin >> Bible:Psalm 109:7]]; the prayer itself is sin. "[[When he seems already fixed, then he is destroyed utterly >> Bible:Job 20:7]]." Like "[[the enemies of the Lord: when they are glorified and exalted, they fail as smoke >> Bible:Psalm 37:20]]." Those who see him — we of the church who see their errors — will say, "Where is he?" "[[Like a dream flown away, he will not be found >> Bible:Job 20:8]]." Such people dream and mold fantasies; they do not rest the mind on truth, and become a dream that cannot be found.

"[[Let lesser ones destroy his sons >> Bible:Job 20:10]]" — sons and disciples of the teacher of these things. "[[Let his hands torch pains >> Bible:Job 20:10]]": the deeds kindle punishment; this impious man’s hands will spend him in last pains — spoken also of the lawless one’s sons. "[[Gall of an asp is in his belly >> Bible:Job 20:14]]:" teachings not sweet but asp gall — the wine of their doctrine. "[[From the vine of Sodom is their vine >> Bible:Deuteronomy 32:32]]." Asp gall sits in the belly of the heterodox and of anyone impious in doctrines opposite the truth.

"[[Wealth gathered unjustly will be vomited out >> Bible:Job 20:15]]." What wealth is that but the wealth in their words? The Good One will not let the fallen keep unjust wealth forever; he makes them vomit it. "[[An angel will drag him from his house >> Bible:Job 20:15]]" — from the badly built house that is a church of evildoers — by God’s energy and kindness. "[[May he not see the milking of pastures >> Bible:Job 20:17]]." The heterodox do not see that milking. Pastures are souls under the good Shepherd: "[[I am the door; if anyone enters through me he will be saved, and will go in and out and find pasture >> Bible:John 10:9]]."

"[[Like tough herb, unchewed, unswallowable >> Bible:Job 20:18]]:" words and doctrines against God are tough and dense, with nothing sweet. As that plant cannot be swallowed even when chewed hard, so the one who wants alien enjoyments carries off no profit from the toil. "[[For this his good things will not bloom >> Bible:Job 20:21]]; when he seems filled, he is afflicted. Belongings cannot buy him salvation. "[[Every necessity will come upon him; wrath of anger is sent >> Bible:Job 20:22]]" — hortatory so we stand off from alien things. Pains come like a snowstorm. "[[He will not be saved from a hand of iron >> Bible:Job 20:24]]": not perceptible iron, but a most cutting word.

choices.choice: Origen maps Job 20 impious to heretic prayer/sacrifice and heterodox doctrines.
Kept cutting-word allegory, not literal iron.
Ends on iron-word; rem continues Job 20 arrows/fire.
